transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2025-11-18
- Start: 15:30 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), David Ortiz (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (CTO - Pulsar), Priya Nair (ML Eng Lead), Samir Gupta (Infra), Jena Park (Product)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i have david here, our solutions engineer. quick intro then we can jump into latency and throughput targets — want to understand what you need for Pulsar Diagnostics.
[00:12] Alex Rivera: cool, yeah thanks. we wanted to talk about p95 latency targets, concurrency — we're instrumenting a realtime triage flow, so p95 is pretty critical. we have a hard SLO at 500ms for p95 on short prompts (<=256 tokens) and softer for longer context.
[00:28] David Ortiz: okay got it, 500ms p95 for short prompts. is that for streaming responses or sync generation?
[00:33] Priya Nair: mostly streaming — we stream tokens back to the UI as they come, so tail latency matters. also we expect bursts during clinician shift changes, roughly 600-1k concurrent sessions, with a baseline of ~150-200.
[00:47] Maya Chen: thanks, that's super helpful. are you currently self-hosting models or using another API?
[00:52] Alex Rivera: we're on a mix — research infra uses managed endpoints from another vendor for experiments, but production we've been trying to self-host on k8s with NVIDIA A10s. cost's spiking and the p95 is inconsistent because of our multiplexing.
[01:06] David Ortiz: right — multiplexing and variable sequence lengths can really affect tail. Redwood has three deployment modes — Hosted (fast onboarding), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), Private (VPC or on-prem). For predictable p95 at scale, customers often pick Dedicated. But we should validate with a benchmark.
[01:24] Samir Gupta: quick question — is p95 measured from request arrival to first token or to completion? we measure both. for the UI we care first token under 500ms.
[01:32] Maya Chen: that's an important distinction — we usually report both. For streaming UX, first-token latency is the key metric. we'll plan benchmarks for both first-token p95 and end-to-end p95.
[01:41] Priya Nair: what about batching? we need to maintain low latency but want batching to reduce cost — how does Redwood balance that?
[01:47] David Ortiz: we use continuous batching and workload-aware batching. you can set latency SLOs that limit batch formation time. Redwood's runtime adjusts kernel selection and can use prefix/KV caching to effectively reduce work for repeated prefixes, which helps hit p95 without blowing cost. note: sometimes auto-transcription calls it KV 'cash' in our logs heh.
[02:05] Jena Park: could you explain KV cache a bit more, because in our tests we saw big variability when users have large context windows and caching wasn't used.
[02:12] David Ortiz: sure — KV cache stores keys/values for attention across tokens so subsequent tokens don't recompute earlier layers for the same context. for chat-like flows where prompt prefixes repeat, it can hugely cut per-token latency. in Dedicated we can pin models and keep KV cache warm across requests from the same session, improving p95.
[02:31] Alex Rivera: sounds promising. what about quantized models? we are considering int4/8 to lower cost but worried about latency and quality tradeoffs.
[02:38] David Ortiz: quantization reduces memory and can increase throughput, but kernel selection matters. Redwood provides quant profiles and recommendations per model. we'll include model/quant recommendations in the benchmark plan.
[02:50] Priya Nair: ok, concrete numbers—what throughput (tokens/sec or req/sec) does Redwood Dedicated show on A100 and A10 for a medium-sized 30B model when aiming at 500ms p95 for first token with streaming?
[03:00] David Ortiz: rough numbers (will validate in POC): on an A100-80GB with optimized kernels and prefix cache, you might see ~200-400 concurrent streaming sessions at 500ms first-token p95 for 30B depending on prompt length and chunking. tokens/sec varies — around 1500-3000 tokens/sec sustained per GPU. on A10 it's lower, maybe 60-120 concurrent sessions for strict 500ms p95. these are ballpark; we'll run your exact traces.
[03:28] Alex Rivera: those ballparks help. our goal is 1k concurrent at peak — looks like Dedicated with multiple GPUs is needed. can Redwood autoscale to handle bursts or does Dedicated have fixed capacity?
[03:38] Maya Chen: Dedicated is reserved but supports autoscale/burst policies — you can configure buffer capacity or allow cross-region fallback to Hosted for overflow. many enterprises do Dedicated primary with Hosted overflow as a graceful degradation strategy.
[03:51] Samir Gupta: fallback to hosted — but then data residency and logs? we cannot send PHI to hosted. privacy constraints are strict.
[03:58] Maya Chen: understood — for PHI you'll want Private (VPC or on-prem). Dedicated can be deployed in your VPC with KMS integration so keys never leave your control; we also support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) / HSM options. we'll share SOC2 + KMS docs.
[04:13] Priya Nair: excellent. next up — benchmarking plan. how do you want traces? we can share per-request token histogram + timestamps.
[04:20] David Ortiz: perfect. ideally we get: sample request traces (timestamps, token counts, client concurrency pattern), representative prompt sets (short, med, long), and any end-to-end client-side timeout settings. we'll provide a runner script and a public benchmark harness — you run it in your env or we can run a Redwood-managed POC in a dedicated pool.
[04:40] Alex Rivera: we prefer Redwood-run in a dedicated pool mimic prod to avoid env differences, but we need to see the exact configs.
[04:46] Maya Chen: we can do that — david will propose a 2-day POC: day 1 sizing runs and smoke tests, day 2 sustained 6-hour run at peak concurrency to collect p95 metrics and token/sec.
[04:57] Jena Park: during POC can we test streaming jitter and first-byte p95 with real browsers?
[05:02] David Ortiz: yes we can include a browser-based client to mimic UI streaming. please note sometimes transcripts/captures show 'speaker 2' and names wrong, so we may need to map session ids; we'll ask for unique session ids in the traces.
[05:15] Priya Nair: any gotchas with TLS termination or load balancers that affect p95? we use an ingress with NLB + TLS offload today.
[05:23] David Ortiz: TLS offload and LB behavior can affect tail, but in Dedicated we recommend keeping TLS at the edge of the cluster matching your topology. we'll include recommended LB configs.
[05:31] Alex Rivera: what about measuring token/sec? we want tokens/sec per GPU and effective tokens/sec per dollar.
[05:37] Maya Chen: we'll provide a token/sec breakdown and cost model — Redwood Console shows token-level cost and latency breakdowns so you can compute tokens/sec per deployment and per model.
[05:47] Samir Gupta: ok. small thing — our infra team wants to ensure RBAC and audit logs for model calls for compliance.
[05:53] Maya Chen: Dedicated and Private offer RBAC, audit logs, and per-call tracing. we'll attach redwood-audit-sample.log and security pack; David will send the SOC2 summary.
[06:02] Priya Nair: what's a realistic timeline for POC? if we agree today can you start next week?
[06:07] Maya Chen: yes, we can kickoff next week pending PO. We usually need sample traces and a quick access setup.
[06:13] Alex Rivera: budget/price ballpark? even rough per-GPU monthly and burst pricing would help.
[06:18] Maya Chen: we'll send a dedicated pricing sheet; typical enterprise contracts for Dedicated start with multi-month commits. for the POC we can offer short-term reserved capacity credits to run the 2-day benchmark.
[06:29] Priya Nair: great. one more — do you do model fallbacks or automatic degradation if p95 spikes?
[06:34] David Ortiz: yes — Redwood supports routing policies and fallback to smaller model variants or quantized profiles; you can set automatic fallback thresholds by latency or load. this helps maintain availability while reducing quality slightly.
[06:45] Jena Park: any limitations on streaming when using fallback? sometimes switching model mid-stream is messy.
[06:50] David Ortiz: we do model-level switching between requests rather than mid-sequence; for active streaming sessions the best practice is to finish the session on the original variant and route new sessions to fallback. we'll include recommended UX patterns.
[07:03] Alex Rivera: ok thanks. i'm concerned about noisy neighbors on Dedicated. how isolated is the pool?
[07:09] Maya Chen: Dedicated provides customer-isolated pools; you control the pool sizing and concurrency caps, so noisy neighbor risk is low. for ultimate isolation, Private on your hardware is the option.
[07:19] Samir Gupta: regarding metrics — can you expose histogram buckets for p50/p95/p99 and raw latency traces to our observability? we use Datadog.
[07:26] David Ortiz: yes we can export to Datadog and provide token-level traces. Redwood Console also has per-route dashboards.
[07:33] Alex Rivera: alright let's recap next steps.
[07:36] Maya Chen: recap: (1) We'll send dedicated pricing, SOC2 and KMS docs, and a proposed 2-day POC plan. (2) David will draft benchmark plan and runner. (3) Pulsar to share sample traces and token histograms. (4) schedule POC kickoff — target next week.
[07:51] Priya Nair: sounds good. I'll try to get the traces by Friday.
[07:55] Maya Chen: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invite and links to the artifacts: latency-benchmark.xlsx, redwood-security-pack.pdf, redwood-audit-sample.log.
[08:06] Alex Rivera: thanks all.

[END OF TRANSCRIPT NOTES]
